results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal

# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

results.title: Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU: what capacity costs | Casitel
highlights:
Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU rates for the H100, H200 and B200, read on 3 November 2026, with published commitment discounts and what else changes the bill.

C Compute · H100 list rates, per GPU-hour Rates read 3 November 2026

$3.99 lowest H100 rate in this note, at Lambda and E2E Networks

Each provider's own page, read 3 November 2026. Not executed prices.

...

## What the rate cards say

All rates below are US dollars per GPU-hour, taken from each provider's own page on 3 November 2026. They are list rates. They are not what large buyers sign.

Provider H100 H200 B200 What the rate is

Lambda$3.99 Not listed$6.69 On-demand, 8-GPU instance

E2E Networks$3.99$5.29$7.99 On-demand

Nebius$4.50$5.40$8.50 On-demand, HGX

CoreWeave$6.16$6.31$8.60 On-demand, North America

AWS$5.97$6.87$14.21 Capacity Blocks, a short reservation

Google Cloud$9.80$10.71 Not read Vertex AI, managed service

Oracle$10.00$10.00$14.00 Pay as you go

Microsoft Azure$12.29 Not read Not read ND H100 v5, East US

Three of these need a note. CoreWeave and Azure price a whole 8-GPU machine by the hour: $49.24 and $98.32 for the H100. The per-GPU figures above are our own arithmetic. AWS publishes a plain on-demand rate only in its calculator, so the AWS row is its Capacity Blocks price, and for the H200 it is the p5e machine (the p5en costs $7.90). Google's row is the Vertex AI managed service, which is not the same product as a bare virtual machine.

Even so, the spread is wide. The H100 runs from $3.99 to $12.29, about three times. The B200 runs from $6.69 to $14.21, about twice. Rate cards also move. In our read on 8 October, Nebius showed $3.85 for an H100. On 3 November it showed $4.50.

## What commitments change

Every provider here says a commitment lowers the rate. Few publish by how much.

C Compute · published commitment discounts Read 3 Nov 2026

E2E Networks 10% to 30%, its own figure

Sakura Internet 5% for 6 months, 10% for 12

Each provider's own pages, read 3 Nov 2026. Discounts off list rates.

- CoreWeave says it offers up to 60% off its on-demand prices for committed use. That is its own claim. The page lists no committed rate.
- Azure publishes reservation prices through its public price API. For the H100 machine in East US, the one-year price works out 36% below pay as you go and the three-year price 56% below. We divided each term price by its hours.
- Google Cloud lists Flexible Savings Plan rates on the Vertex AI page. For the H200 they are $9.64 for one year and $8.57 for three, which is 10% and 20% below $10.71.
- E2E Networks says three-month, six-month and annual commitments can earn 10% to 30%, depending on length and volume.
- Sakura Internet announced on 1 July 2026 a commitment plan for one H100 plan: 5% off for six months and 10% off for twelve.
- AWS cut P5 (H100) prices by 44% for on-demand and 45% for the three-year Instance Savings Plan from 1 June 2025. Those are cuts from its earlier prices, not discounts off today's rate.
- Nebius and Lambda name no percentage. Both point large buyers to sales.

Nebius prints the rates in its document Compute pricing in Nebius AI Cloud. The page says on-demand prices for B300, B200, H200, and H100 changed on 1 October 2026, and that from 8 October 2026 the preemptible price on several of those platforms is a dynamic spot rate, displayed as a floor. The dollar figures on that page are before tax. The billing unit is one second and the pricing unit is one hour, so thirty minutes is half the hourly rate. A stopped virtual machine is not charged for the GPU. The bars are the on-demand rates read on 10 October 2026. The 8 October note on that page is a preemptible floor, and it is not drawn. The line above the bars is what an H100 hour has cost across the months a posted rate could be read.

NVIDIA B300 NVLink is 9.50 dollars for one GPU-hour, with a preemptible floor of 0.99 dollars. Before 1 October the same block lists 7.85 dollars on demand. NVIDIA B200 NVLink is 8.50 dollars for one GPU-hour. The page ties one platform id to us-central1 and another to me-west1, at the same on-demand rate, with a preemptible floor of 0.99 dollars. Before 1 October that block lists 7.15 dollars. NVIDIA H200 NVLink is 5.40 dollars, in eu-north1, eu-north2, eu-west1, and us-central1, with a preemptible floor of 0.79 dollars. Before 1 October it lists 4.50 dollars. NVIDIA H100 NVLink is 4.50 dollars, and the page says that platform is only in eu-north1. The preemptible floor is 0.79 dollars. Before 1 October it lists 3.85 dollars.

...

Lambda's instance page, opened the same day, lists the chip, the onboard memory, the vCPUs, and a price per GPU-hour, plus applicable tax. The B200 SXM6 row with 180 GB and 208 vCPUs is 6.69 dollars. The H100 SXM row with 80 GB and 208 vCPUs is 3.99 dollars. The A100 SXM row with 80 GB and 240 vCPUs is 2.79 dollars. The page groups further rows under smaller instance sizes. B200 SXM6 appears again at 6.79, 6.89, and 6.99 dollars, next to 104, 52, and 26 vCPUs. H100 SXM on those rows is 4.09, 4.19, and 4.29 dollars. An H100 PCIe row with 80 GB and 26 vCPUs is 3.29 dollars. A GH200 row with 96 GB is 2.29 dollars. Under the B200 section the page says the instances start at 6.69 dollars, and it says the part offers up to three times the training and fifteen times the inference of H100. It does not say how many tokens that hour produces.

...

A spot floor is not the on-demand rate. Nebius says the preemptible price can change as often as every fifteen minutes, that it stays at least one cent under the on-demand rate, and that the number on the documentation page is a minimum. The phrase is "from 0.79" or "from 0.99", not the charge a running job will see. The on-demand column is the figure a reader can compare next month without logging into a console.

An H100 hour has not moved in one smooth line, and the two rates on the chart are different offers. The SXM5 pay-as-you-go hour was $4.85 from November 2023 through July 2024, and $3.50 on 15 September 2024. The later NVLink hour was $2.95 from October 2025 through May 2026, $3.85 from 1 June 2026, and $4.50 from 1 October 2026. The months between September 2024 and November 2025 are left empty. The posted offer changed, and those in-between months were not in the copies read for this brief. A third quote, $2.118 for the GPU alone with the processor and memory billed beside it, is not drawn.

The useful update is the dated move on the Nebius page itself. From 1 October 2026 the on-demand H100 line goes from 3.85 to 4.50 dollars, the H200 line from 4.50 to 5.40, the B200 line from 7.15 to 8.50, and the B300 line from 7.85 to 9.50. Those four pairs are on one document, with the old rate left in place under a "before" heading. Lambda's instance rows do not carry a date. The 6.69 and 3.99 dollar figures are what that URL showed on 10 October 2026, and a revision should open the URL again rather than treat them as a contract.

Median of each provider's median advertised on-demand price. Chips with fewer providers move more from week to week.

## Two prices for the same hour

Published rate cards tell a different story from marketplaces. Our price board — built from the on-demand prices cloud providers publish — put the on-demand H100 hour at $4.11 on 13 Nov 2026, against a marketplace median of $3.93 in the week of 9 Nov 2026.

Neither number is “the” price. List prices show what providers ask for capacity on demand; marketplace medians show where spare capacity clears; reserved and contract prices, usually lower again, sit in agreements that are rarely published in full. For anyone valuing a neocloud, lending against GPUs or underwriting a datacentre lease, the spread between the three says how tight capacity is.

### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

results.title: AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at
results.author: Paul Nugent
highlights:
Paul Nugent

Nov 4, 2026

AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at the same price.

This is the most important AI infrastructure pricing story of the year, and the signal is unmistakable.

The move: ~20% price increase on EC2 Capacity Block reservations for Nvidia GPU instances, effective July 1. AWS cited "supply and demand dynamics" — meaning the global compute crunch has gotten severe enough that AWS believes customers will pay more without leaving.

The critical detail: Trainium pricing is unchanged.

AWS now operates two parallel compute economics tracks:

🔹 NVIDIA TRACK: +20% — you absorb Nvidia's pricing power, supply constraints, AND AWS's margin protection layered on top.

🔹 TRAINIUM TRACK: flat — Amazon subsidizes the economics because every workload that migrates to Trainium deepens lock-in to the AWS ecosystem.

results.title: RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99
results.author: TSN Newsroom
highlights:
RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99

# RunPod’s Secure Cloud GPU Rates Have Risen: H100 SXM Now $3.99 an Hour, B200 $7.99, a Tracker Reports

October 10, 2026

Illustration.

A GPU price tracker, GPU Economy, says RunPod raised 12 of its 29 on-demand Secure Cloud GPU rates on 8 October 2026 [1]. RunPod’s pricing page now shows the higher prices [2]. RunPod made no announcement that we could find, so the timing and the old prices rest on the tracker.

## The new rates

RunPod sells two tiers, Secure Cloud and Community Cloud; on its listings the Community rates are lower. Prices are in US dollars per GPU per hour, on demand, meaning pay as you go. GPU Economy reports [1]:

| GPU | Before | Now | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.49 | $3.99 | +14.3% |
| H200 | $4.59 | $5.29 | +15.3% |
| B200 | $6.79 | $7.99 | +17.7% |
| B300 | $7.89 | $8.99 | +13.9% |

The H100, H200, B200 and B300 are Nvidia data-centre chips used to train and run AI models. The tracker says the 12 rises came “between our reads of October 8, 2026 at 15:41 and 16:41 UTC”, which is 16:41 and 17:41 in London. It also computes that one H100 SXM running for a 730-hour month went from $2,547.70 to $2,912.70.

## What did not change

The tracker says “None of the 35 Community Cloud on-demand rates changed in the same read”: the H100 SXM there stayed at $2.69 and the B200 at $5.98 [1].

## What RunPod’s page shows

RunPod’s pricing page lists $3.99/hr for the H100 SXM, $7.99/hr for the B200, $5.29/hr for the H200 and $8.99/hr for the B300 [2]. But the page is labelled “Updated September 27, 2026”, which does not match the tracker’s 8 October timing. The page’s hidden structured data, the code search engines read, still lists the old Secure Cloud prices, such as $3.49 for the H100 SXM [2]. The tracker says it read RunPod’s public API, and that on 9 October the page’s own markup still carried $3.49 [1]. That fits what we see.

## What this does not show

- A RunPod announcement. We found none, and no reason for the rises.
- When RunPod made the change. The tracker reads hourly and gives a one-hour window.
- Other providers’ prices. This covers RunPod only.
- Every region or product. Serverless and cluster pricing are not covered.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
Every month we check the public on-demand prices of specialist GPU clouds to set our own: CoreGPU prices every GPU at least 25% below the market median. This is the data behind that number, as listed on November 4, 2026.

## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

...

## Hyperscalers

On-demand prices per GPU-hour at the largest clouds remain far above specialist clouds: H100 from $6.88 (8-GPU instance divided by eight) to more than $12 depending on the provider, and B300 from $15 to $17.80. Commitments of one to three years cut those prices by 30 to 56%.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.
